a: A clustered index defines physical row order (often the primary key).
A covering index can satisfy a query from the index alone.
High selectivity columns (many distinct values) benefit more from indexes.
Leftmost prefix rule: (a,b,c) helps a, a+b, a+b+c filters.
Index-only scans read from the index without heap fetches when possible.
Partial indexes cover a subset of rows matching a WHERE clause.
Expression/functional indexes speed queries on computed expressions.
Index bloat wastes space and slows scans; reindex/vacuum as needed.
Each extra index speeds reads but slows inserts/updates/deletes.
Use EXPLAIN to verify Index Scan vs Seq Scan decisions.
